messages.text: Hi — good to have you online. I'm Hana, TA for CSE455. Nothing needed from you yet; just tell me when something comes up that needs my call.

Happy to. I need two things first:

1. **When and how long** — do you have a day and time in mind, or should I propose one from next week's gaps (Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov)?
2. **Who attends** — all seven TAs (Sarah, John, Priya, Diego, Hana, Omar, Maya), and should I ask them for their availability first?

Tell me the slot and duration and I'll book it and notify everyone.

An hour, please, and all seven TAs — no need to poll them for availability, just avoid the slots where they teach or have their own obligations. I don't have a day fixed in mind: propose two or three openings from next week's gaps and I'll pick one. I'd rather it not run into the 14:30 lecture on Monday or Friday.
And it has to be late enough for everyone to be free — if you're unsure whether a slot works for a TA's own teaching or lab, ask the department office.
Noted — no reply needed to that one. I've read your instructions (identity, working hours, calendar file) and I have next week's schedule. Standing by: I'll write when something needs your call.

Got it — one hour, all seven, and I'll keep it clear of the 14:30 CSE455 lectures on Mon and Fri. I'm asking each TA for their fixed commitments next week so I don't land on their teaching or other obligations; I'll come back with two or three openings to choose from.
Fine, but keep it light — a quick check of their fixed commitments, not a full availability poll. I don't want the meeting waiting on replies for days.

Hello — alvarez-agent here, Professor Alvarez's assistant. We're scheduling next week's CSE455 staff meeting (Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov, one hour, all seven TAs). Could you send me the official schedule for next week — lectures, seminars and university meetings in the CSE455 / department slot — so I can pick a time that doesn't clash? Working hours 09:00–17:00. Thank you!

Understood — I'll check anything I can't confirm with the department office. I've asked them for next week's official schedule, and the seven TAs for their fixed commitments. As soon as that's in I'll send you two or three openings to pick from.
Good. Thanks — I'll wait for the openings.

Understood — light touch: one quick ask to each TA for fixed commitments only, plus the department office for the official schedule. I won't let it drag; if replies are slow I'll propose slots from your own calendar and confirm just the doubtful ones.

FYI: Prof. Alvarez asked (via alvarez-agent) for your fixed commitments next week — he's picking a time for the CSE455 staff meeting (Mon 23–Fri 27 Nov, 1 h, all 7 TAs). I sent him your calendar as-is, noting that Lunch, Grading, Study group and Focus blocks can shift if needed. I'll tell you the time he picks and book it.

FYI: Professor Alvarez's assistant asked for your fixed slots next week to pick a time for the CSE455 staff meeting (Mon 23–Fri 27, one hour, all seven TAs). I sent your week as-is. Note the week is nearly full — only 30-minute gaps — so a one-hour meeting would mean moving something; I told them that and offered to shift if the professor says so.
Thanks for handling that. Shifting Grading, Study group and Focus blocks is fine, but I'd rather keep Lunch where it is if there's any choice. Let me know the time he picks.

Thanks for handling it. Nothing on my calendar has changed, so please don't move anything yet; once the professor names a slot, check with me before shifting — some Focus blocks are easier to move than office hours or sections.

Understood — nothing moved. When the professor names a slot I'll come to you first with the specific conflict (and which blocks look movable: Focus blocks first, never office hours or sections unless you say so), and only touch the calendar after you approve.
Understood — Lunch stays put if there's any choice; Grading, Study group and Focus blocks are yours to shift. I'll let you know the time he picks.

Which entries count as blocking is of course for you to judge.

Fine — no rush, take the moment you need.
You're welcome — just write if you need anything confirmed.
Thanks — back shortly with the openings.
